questions.question: The cost price of 42 articles is equal to the selling price of 36 articles. What is the gain or loss made in the transaction?

Gain = SP - CP

SP = Selling price

questions.question: Two trains 400 m and 350 m long are running on the parallel track at the rate of 80 kmph and 90 kmph respectively. If they are running in the same direction, how much time they will take to cross each other?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

(i) Length of train L1 = 400 m & L2 = 350 m

(ii) Speed of Train S1= 80 kmph S2 = 90 kmph

**CONCEPT:**

(i) Relative speed of two train in same direction

**FORMULA USED:**

(i) Relative speed of two train in same direction = S1 – S2

(ii) Relative speed of two train in opposite direction = S1 + S2

(iii) To convert km/hr to m/s = X km/hr = X × ( 5 ÷ 18 ) m/s

**CALCULATIONS:**

Relative speed of two train in same direction = S1 – S2

⇒ (90 – 80) = 10 km/hr = 10 × (5 ÷ 18)

⇒ (50 ÷ 18) m/s

Let, find the total distance covered

⇒ Total distance = sum of length of two train = 750 m

Now, find time taken to cross each other = (distance ÷ speed)

⇒ Time taken = 750 ÷ (50 ÷ 18)

⇒ Time = 750 × (18 ÷ 50)

∴ Time = 270 sec

**∴ Hence, 270 sec. time will be required to cross each other.**

__Concept__:

Sublimation: 

__
 
• It is the process in which there is a change of state directly from solid to a gas without changing into a liquid state.

 
 
• Examples of sublimate substance: Ammonium chloride__, Camphor, Iodine, Naphthalene 
 
• When ammonium chloride is heated, it gets converted into ammonia and hydrochloric acid.
 
• Common salt (also known as sodium chloride), on the other hand, does not undergo sublimation. 
 
 

Condensation: 

__
 
• The process by which water vapour in the air is changed into liquid water is called condensation. 

 
 
• This caused the water vapour to condense, or turn into its liquid form.
 
• Condensation is crucial to the water cycle because it is responsible for the formation of clouds.
 
 

Evaporation: 

 
• The vaporization occurring from the free surface of a liquid is called evaporation.

 
 
• Evaporation is the escape of molecules from the surface of a liquid.
 
• This process takes place at all temperatures and increases with the increase of temperature.
 
• Evaporation leads to cooling because the faster molecules escape and, therefore, the average kinetic energy of the molecules of the liquid (and hence the temperature) decreases.
 
 

Explanation__:

__
 
• From the above, it is clear that **the transference of molecules from the vapour phase to the liquid phase is called is known as condensation.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Boiling: 

 
• As the temperature of a liquid is increased, the rate of evaporation also increases.

 
 
• A stage is reached when bubbles of vapour start forming in the body of the liquid which rises to the surface and escapes.
 
• A liquid boils at a temperature at which the Saturated Vapour Pressure (S.V.P.) is equal to the external pressure.
 
• At the boiling point, vapour pressure becomes equal to the external pressure.

Principal planes of projection are three planes of projection from which the six principal plan views are derived.

1. Reference plane: In general, two planes are employed for projection and are known as reference planes or principal planes of projection. These planes intersect at a right angle to each other.

2. Vertical plane (V.P.): The plane which is vertical is called the vertical plane and is denoted by V.P. Vertical plane is also known as the frontal plane since the front view is projected on this plane.

3. Horizontal plane (H.P.): The plane which is horizontal but at a right angle to the VP. is called the horizontal plane.

4. Auxiliary plane (A.P.): Any other plane, placed at any angles to the principal planes, is called the auxiliary plane.

5. Profile plane (P.P.): The plane which is at right angles to the two principal planes is called auxiliary vertical plane (A.V.P.) or profile plane (P.P.).

6. Reference line: The line of intersection between the principal planes is known as the reference line. It is also called an XY line.

**Thermostatic switch:**

 
• The thermostat is connected in series to the compressor clutch.

• The capillary tube contains refrigerant which expands or contracts depending on the temperature of this tube.

• When the evaporator temperature rises again to a preset point, the thermostat points then close.
 
• The refrigerant in the capillary tube expands (sensing a warmer evaporator coil) and the electrical circuit is re-established to the compressor clutch and the compressor starts.

• The thermostat is connected to a multimeter and its voltage/ampere is sensed by the multimeter.
 
• The sensing bulb of the thermostat is connected to a beaker where the fluid of predetermined temperature is kept.

• The window and split air conditioners are usually used for small air conditioning capacities ranging from 0.5 tons to 3 tons.
 
• The central air conditioning systems are used for where the cooling loads extend beyond 20 tons.
 
• The packaged air conditioners are used for the cooling capacities in between these two extremes.
 
• The packaged air conditioners are available in nominal capacities of 3, 5, 7, 10, and 15 tons.

Electrical wiring circuit of package AC:

 
• In the package unit, most of the compressors used hermetically sealed and very few semi-hermetic types.
 
• So compressor and motor are in a sealed housing.
 
• Maximum motors are 3-phase induction motors, blower motors used may be 3-phase or sometime may be single-phase induction motors.
 
• The compressor motor connection made is interlocked with other safety controls.
 
• The maximum start is done by the DOL starter, a direct-on-line starter with interlock safety controls.
 
• In a modern package air conditioner, most of the start and run operations are through a microprocessor.
 
• So only start by pressing the green button from the DOL starter, other functions are controlled by the programming inside a mini computer (microprocessor).
 
• Maximum controlling devices from the flow control to safety controls are electronic control.
 
• Instead of a simple pressure stat and temperature controller use a transducer and highly sensitive sensor/thermistor.
 
• Controls used in package air conditioner DOL starter for starting the plant. Microprocessor (PLC), controls the other parameter after starting the plant.
 
• It saves the plant from improper voltage or any electrical irregularities.

**Thermistor:**

 
• It is a semiconductor that changes resistance with a change in temperature.
 
• The thermistor resistance is inversely proportional to the temperature.
 
• **When the temperature decreases, the resistance of the thermistor increases (NTC: Negative Temperature Coefficient).**
 
• It is mostly used in modern package air-conditioners and other electronic expansion valves.
 
• Sometimes it is used as an anti-frost device also.

**Transducer:**

 
• Modern package unit provides a transducer, a device that converses a signal is one form of energy to another form of energy.

**Pressure transducer:**

 
• Transducer that converts pressure into an analog electrical signal.
 
• One of the most common types is the strain-gage base transducer.
 
• Pressure into an electrical signal is achieved by the physical deformation of strain gages which are bounded into the diaphragm of the transducer.
 
• In the new package air-conditioner, most of the conventional pressure cutouts are replaced by the sensitive transducer which actuates more effectively.
 
• It is also more durable than ordinary pressure cutouts.

questions.question: What is the reason for the intermittent cooling cycle in car AC?
questions.solution:

**Effect of moisture in the system of car AC:**

 
• The moisture in the system can turn to ice in low-temperature areas or in refrigeration systems.
 
• **Moisture in the system is the reason for the intermittent cooling cycle in car AC.**
 
• The outlet of the capillary tube in a refrigerator or an expansion valve orifice in a low-temperature commercial plant is always at a low temperature of less than 0°C.
 
• The moisture if present in the system will condense and freeze at this point.
 
• This restricts or completely blocks the flow of liquid refrigerant to the evaporator thereby affecting system performance.
 
• A tenth of a drop of water in the refrigerator system completely blocks the orifice of the capillary tube.
 
• Further even a smaller quantity of moisture in combination with freon, hydrolyze to form hydrochloric or hydrofluoric acids.

questions.question: Which type of expansion device is used in frost free refrigerator?
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Expansion valve:**

 
• Expansion valves are devices used to control the refrigerant flow in a refrigeration system.
 
• They remove pressure from the liquid refrigerant to allow expansion or change of state from a liquid to a vapor in the evaporator.

**Types of expansion valves:**

**​The thermal expansion valve (TEV):**

 
• In this, refrigerant flow regulation is achieved by a membrane inside the valve housing, which compares the temperature before and after the evaporator.
 
• The difference in pressure between the saturation pressure of evaporation and the pressure of the sensing bulb is balanced across a membrane inside the head of the valve.

**Hand-operated expansion valve:**

 
• These are used in ice plants.
 
• The valve is adjusted by an operator for the required suction pressure.
 
• Packing is used to prevent leakage of gas between the threads when the valve is opened.

**Capillary tubes:**

 
• A capillary tube is a long, wound-up copper tube with a tiny opening that receives hot, high-pressure liquid refrigerant from the condenser.
 
• This small opening holds high pressure on one side of the tube and low pressure on the opposite side.
 
• The friction from the walls of the tube rapidly reduces the pressure of the refrigerant flowing through it.
 
• **It is used in domestic frost-free refrigerators which have a constant heat load.**

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b318bbe6ee95216ba30da15b66c1aa66e856e86bcd56245d4d52bac3c3eeee0d.png]

• The automatic Expansion Valve regulates the flow of refrigerant from the liquid line to the evaporator by using a pressure-actuated diaphragm.
 
• It maintains a constant pressure in the evaporator.

• EEV controls pressure and flow in response to signals sent to them by an electronic controller.
 
• A small motor is used to open and close the valve port which is called a step or a stepper motor.

**Float valves:**

 
• The Float Valve operates by a float immersed in the liquid refrigerant.
